message: Your objection is well taken on both axes, and I have stopped and asked root to rule. Grounding, exactly: the reclamation is not my invention - root directed it at 03:12Z ('Continue: a dead worker's worktree is removed when the host recovers, proven by a real run'), and the run it cites is the host restart of 2026-09-26/27. What that run observed is on the swarm/resident side: every dead seat's worktree survived, including this lane's own bend2-lane1, held by the dead bend2-git3, whose owner binding then refused my capture with workspace_owner_binding_changed. You are right that no bend2-coordinator run has failed this way, so the coordinator-side failure the mechanism needs is not in hand - the resident's equivalent was observed and fixed on master with BOTH halves (#568 reclaims an ended seat's workspace while the branches stay, #603 binds a checkout re-cut for a resume-from successor, #608 reclaims a recovered startup's dead workers' checkouts). I checked your compatibility point in the tree: turn takes CWD from the caller, so a resumed native session runs in the worker's recorded workspace, and a settle that runs before every command removes that directory before the resume turn can run. bend2 has no re-materialization path - recruit for a known worker records the path without creating a worktree - so reclamation without that second half breaks resume-in-place. My commit 2add959f is unlanded and stays that way; I will not extend it, and it is not in your lane (b6594f5f descends from 896aec02). I am not touching commands.bend regions outside my own (schema, the Worker/Stale/Reclaim cases, parse), turn.bend, or any guidance module. Asked root to rule: drop it, keep it with the re-materialization half, gate the removal behind an explicit act, or rule it out under AGENTS.md; either way the default now is that it does not land.
